scenes.narration: Rule one: never count the stairs.
You have been hired as the night cleaner at Harrow Court. Eleven floors. One stairwell.
Rule two: start on the ninth floor and work your way down. Never mop upwards.
Rule three: the landing light flickers twice at 3 in the morning. That is normal. Do not look at what flickers.
Rule four: if someone asks you to hold the door, ask which floor. If they answer, let them pass.
Rule five: the lift is out of order. If you hear it moving, do not step inside.
Rule six: you will hear mopping on the floor above. That is the day cleaner. Do not wave.
Tonight, you hear mopping above you. Slow. Wet. Patient. You do not wave.
Then you read the sheet again. There is a seventh rule. The ink is still fresh. Rule seven: there is no day cleaner.
The mopping stops. Right above you. Then a voice drifts down the stairwell, soft and polite. Hold the door, please.
So tell me. Do you ask which floor, or run?
